ctx.error: EXIT-10: more than one change described for a single pilot (matrix §4a trigger: "pilot plan declares more than one change"). The Improve loop is one-change-at-a-time by design (PLAN §4.1, rubric R-IMP-02 #1): run the extra change as its own sequential pilot once this one is proven, declare a genuinely inseparable PACKAGE explicitly if the components truly cannot deploy apart (R-IMP-02's carve-out -- attribution then goes to the package only, never a component), or route to the advisor / v1.1 Experiment Planner / a human expert for a real multi-factor question. Remove the extra entry from `changes` (got 2) before saving.

analysis_plan.rationale: Two independent windows of continuous handoff minutes, n=120 each -- different orders, different customers, nobody measured twice. Welch's t is the engine's two-independent-means default (no shared-variance assumption). A forecast, not a lock: T-20 routes the real data itself.

changes.text: Batch milk steaming with marked-cup sequencing at the drink-build step: scan the next three marked cups for a same-milk pair before each build, pull both drinks' shots back-to-back while one shared pitcher steams, and build cups strictly in ticket order from a marked front-of-rail position.
An extra bundled change, proving EXIT-10 fires.

comparison_design.description: The frozen Measure baseline, named exactly: wait-times.csv, every-4th-order sampling, 10 weekday mornings 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-31, n=120, mean 8.408, sd 1.042, engine-verified stable (0 rule-1/rule-4 signals). The pilot window mirrors it: 10 weekday mornings 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-21, same 7:00-10:00 peak, 12 sampled orders per morning, 6 per daypart.

demand.note: Summer-session demand has held near the baseline's 48 orders per peak all July; daily order counts will be recorded through the pilot (the charter's mitigation) and re-checked at proof.

measurement.note: Same operational definition (register order-paid stamp to name call, tenths of a minute), same POS wall clock, same tally sheet; the T-12 measurement check (repeatability 8.94%, acceptable) still stands and nothing about the instrument changes.

other.note: No menu, price, or layout changes scheduled in the window; the espresso machine's annual service is booked for late September, after both planned pilot rounds. FMEA actions already in flight (queue-rail labels, register read-back) predate the pilot window and run in both periods.

season.note: Both windows sit inside summer session; fall semester begins 2026-08-31, after the pilot ends -- the window was placed to keep it out.

staffing.note: Same morning crew as the baseline window -- Priya on register/lead, Marcus and Riley rotating the espresso station; no hires, departures, or schedule changes planned through 2026-08-21.

input.falsification_line: If the pilot-window mean over the full 10 mornings (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-21) is not below 7.0 minutes, batching did not move the queue -- revert to single-drink build, log the reversion, and take the next-ranked fix to its own pilot.

inclusion.honesty_note: This is the crew and counter we have: one site, no randomization, and the same two baristas as the baseline. The window is summer session by design -- it ends 2026-08-21, before fall semester starts 2026-08-31, so the charter's demand confound stays out of round 1. What convenience costs us: nothing here says the change works on a different crew or a semester-load morning.
inclusion.how_selected: Same systematic every-4th-order rule as the baseline, same tally sheet, same POS-clock operational definition -- selection method held identical so the two windows compare like for like
inclusion.who_or_what: All espresso-drink orders at the campus coffee bar during the weekday 7:00-10:00 peak, both baristas (Marcus, Riley), every 4th espresso order sampled -- 12 per morning, 6 per daypart, exactly the T-11 collection plan's rule

input.notes: Round-1 pilot of the T-18 ranked list's #1 fix (sol-batch-steam), designed and saved 2026-08-07 -- threshold, falsification line, and confounder answers all entered before the first pilot morning (2026-08-10); status flipped to complete when the window closed 2026-08-21. One change only: a draft with the grinder dial-in added as a second change was refused by the engine with EXIT-10 named in the error, and the grinder change went back to the queue as round 2 -- the refusal run is recorded in improve-run.md. The pilot window is 10 weekday mornings, 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-21, deliberately ending before fall semester starts (the charter's confound risk); sampling, operational definition, and measurement system are the baseline's own, unchanged.
